## Why This Is Asked

Tests practical ability to design end-to-end CI/CD for per-PR isolation, secret management, health checks, and cleanup.

## Key Concepts

- YAML pipelines
- Matrix strategy
- Containerization and ACR
- Helm/Kubernetes
- Azure Key Vault

## Code Example

```yaml
trigger:
  branches:
    include:
      - '**'
pool:
  vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
variables:
  registry: 'myacr.azurecr.io'
  imageName: 'flask-api'
  prNamespace: 'pr-${{ env.SYSTEM_PULLREQUEST_PULLREQUESTID }}'
jobs:
- job: BuildTest
  displayName: 'Build and test'
  strategy:
    matrix:
      Python39: { pythonVersion: '3.9' }
      Python311: { pythonVersion: '3.11' }
  steps:
  - task: UsePythonVersion@0
    inputs:
      versionSpec: '$(pythonVersion)'
  - script: python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
    displayName: 'Install deps'
  - script: pytest
    displayName: 'Run tests'
  - script: flake8
    displayName: 'Lint'
  - script: |
      docker build -t $(registry)/$(imageName):$(Build.BuildId) .
    displayName: 'Build image'
  - script: |
      docker push $(registry)/$(imageName):$(Build.BuildId)
    displayName: 'Push image'
  - script: |
      helm upgrade --install flask-api chart --namespace $(prNamespace) --set image.tag=$(Build.BuildId)
    displayName: 'Deploy to AKS'
  - script: |
      curl -sS http://flask-api.$(prNamespace).svc.cluster.local/health || exit 1
    displayName: 'Health check'
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you adapt this for multiple PRs running concurrently?
- What failure modes would you guard against and how would you monitor them?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests PR validation knowledge, per-PR configuration management, secret handling in CI/CD pipelines, container image workflows, and security gates.

## Key Concepts
- PR validation with Azure Pipelines YAML
- Python 3.11 with dependency caching
- Azure Key Vault integration in pipelines
- Azure App Configuration for per-PR settings overrides
- Docker image build and push to ACR
- Health checks and merge gates
- Lightweight security scanning in CI

## Code Example
```yaml
trigger: none
pr:
  branches:
    include:
      - main
  paths:
    include:
      - src/**
      - tests/**
      - Dockerfile
      - azure-pipelines.yml

variables:
  pythonVersion: '3.11'
  dockerRegistryServiceConnection: 'acr-connection'
  imageName: 'fastapi-service'
  imageTag: '$(Build.BuildId)'

stages:
- stage: Validate
  displayName: 'Validate PR'
  jobs:
  - job: Test
    displayName: 'Run Tests'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    steps:
    - task: UsePythonVersion@0
      inputs:
        versionSpec: '$(pythonVersion)'

    - task: Cache@2
      inputs:
        key: 'pip | $(Agent.OS) | requirements.txt'
        path: '$(Pipeline.Workspace)/.pip'
      displayName: 'Cache pip dependencies'

    - script: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        pip install -r requirements.txt
      displayName: 'Install dependencies'

    - task: AzureKeyVault@2
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: 'azure-service-connection'
        KeyVaultName: 'kv-name'
        SecretsFilter: '*'
        RunAsPreJob: false

    - task: AzureAppConfiguration@1
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: 'azure-service-connection'
        AppConfigurationEndpoint: 'https://appconfig-name.azconfig.io'
        Label: 'pr-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestId)'
        KeyValueFilters: 'test-*'

    - script: |
        pytest tests/ -v --junitxml=$(Build.StagingDirectory)/test-results.xml
      displayName: 'Run unit tests'
      continueOnError: true

    - publish: $(Build.StagingDirectory)/test-results.xml
      artifact: test-results
      displayName: 'Publish test results'

- stage: BuildAndScan
  displayName: 'Build Image & Scan'
  dependsOn: Validate
  jobs:
  - job: Build
    displayName: 'Build & Push Docker Image'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    steps:
    - task: Docker@2
      displayName: 'Build and push image to ACR'
      inputs:
        containerRegistry: '$(dockerRegistryServiceConnection)'
        repository: '$(imageName)'
        tags: '$(imageTag)'
        command: 'buildAndPush'
        Dockerfile: '$(Build.SourcesDirectory)/Dockerfile'

  - job: HealthCheck
    displayName: 'Health Check Container'
    dependsOn: Build
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    steps:
    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Deploy container for testing'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: 'azure-service-connection'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          az container create \
            --resource-group rg-name \
            --name healthcheck-$(Build.BuildId) \
            --image $(dockerRegistryServiceConnection).azurecr.io/$(imageName):$(imageTag) \
            --cpu 1 --memory 1 \
            --ports 8000

          az container wait \
            --resource-group rg-name \
            --name healthcheck-$(Build.BuildId) \
            --condition Running

    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Verify health endpoint'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: 'azure-service-connection'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          sleep 10
          curl -f http://localhost:8000/health || exit 1

    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Cleanup container'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: 'azure-service-connection'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          az container delete \
            --resource-group rg-name \
            --name healthcheck-$(Build.BuildId) \
            --yes

  - job: SecurityScan
    displayName: 'Trivy Security Scan'
    dependsOn: Build
    steps:
    - task: Trivy@0
      inputs:
        scanType: 'fs'
        scanPath: '$(Build.SourcesDirectory)'
        format: 'table'
        severity: 'CRITICAL,HIGH'
        exitCode: '1'
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests knowledge of Azure Pipelines matrix builds, caching strategy, and cache invalidation tied to lockfiles—crucial for reliable PR speed.

## Key Concepts

- Azure Pipelines matrix strategy for Node versions
- Cache@2 task and cache key composition
- npm ci vs npm install in CI
- Cache invalidation via package-lock.json

## Code Example

```yaml
trigger:
- '**/*'
pr:
- '*'
pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest

variables:
  npmCache: '$(Pipeline.Workspace)/.npm'

strategy:
  matrix:
    Node14:
      NodeVersion: '14'
    Node16:
      NodeVersion: '16'

steps:
- task: UseNode@1
  inputs:
    versionSpec: '$(NodeVersion)'
  displayName: 'Use Node.js $(NodeVersion)'

- task: Cache@2
  inputs:
    key: 'npm | $(Agent.OS) | package-lock.json'
    restoreKeys: |
      npm | $(Agent.OS)
    path: '~/.npm'
  displayName: 'Cache npm'

- script: npm ci
  displayName: 'Install dependencies'

- script: npm test
  displayName: 'Run tests'
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This evaluates expertise in designing production-grade, GitOps-driven CI/CD pipelines that create isolated, ephemeral environments for pull requests while maintaining security, compliance, and cost efficiency.

## Key Concepts
- Selective builds based on path detection in monorepos
- PR-scoped container tagging and Azure Container Registry integration
- Managed identity authentication with Azure Key Vault
- Policy enforcement through Kyverno validation gates
- Ephemeral environments with automatic cleanup and TTL management
- GitOps reconciliation and drift prevention using FluxCD
- End-to-end testing with isolated staging databases
- Comprehensive observability via Azure Monitor with cost controls

## Code Example
```yaml
# azure-pipelines.yml - PR-driven ephemeral deployment pipeline
trigger:
  none
pr:
  branches:
    include:
    - main

variables:
  - group: azure-infrastructure
  - name: prNumber
    value: $(System.PullRequest.PullRequestNumber)
  - name: prTag
    value: 'pr-$(prNumber)'

stages:
- stage: DetectChanges
  displayName: 'Detect Changed Services'
  jobs:
  - job: detect
    steps:
    - bash: |
        git diff origin/main --name-only > changed_files.txt
        echo "##vso[task.setvariable variable=changedServices;isOutput=true]$(python detect-services.py changed_files.txt)"
      name: detect

- stage: BuildAndPush
  displayName: 'Build and Push Services'
  dependsOn: DetectChanges
  condition: succeeded()
  jobs:
  - job: build
    strategy:
      matrix: $[ stageDependencies.DetectChanges.detect.outputs['detect.changedServices'] ]
    steps:
    - task: Docker@2
      inputs:
        containerRegistry: $(acrServiceConnection)
        repository: $(service.name)
        tags: |
          $(prTag)
          $(Build.BuildNumber)
        command: buildAndPush
        Dockerfile: $(service.path)/Dockerfile
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Ephemeral PR environments are a cornerstone of modern DevOps practices, enabling teams to validate changes in isolated environments without affecting production. This question assesses the candidate's understanding of Kubernetes lifecycle management, infrastructure-as-code practices, and observability in cloud-native deployments.

## Key Concepts
- PR-triggered ephemeral environments for isolated testing
- Kubernetes namespaces dynamically provisioned per PR
- Helm-based application deployments
- End-to-end smoke testing in isolated environments
- Automated teardown with policy safeguards and comprehensive logging

## Code Example
```yaml
trigger: none
pr:
  branches:
    include:
    - main
  paths:
    include:
    - src/**
    - charts/**
    - azure-pipelines.yml

variables:
  PR_NUMBER: $(System.PullRequest.PullRequestNumber)
  NAMESPACE: 'pr-$(PR_NUMBER)'
  RETENTION_HOURS: 24
  AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION: 'Azure-Production'
  AKS_CLUSTER: 'aks-cluster-01'
  RESOURCE_GROUP: 'rg-aks-prod'

stages:
- stage: Provision
  displayName: 'Provision Ephemeral Environment'
  jobs:
  - job: CreateNamespace
    displayName: 'Create PR Namespace'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    steps:
    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Create AKS Namespace'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          az aks get-credentials \
            --resource-group $(RESOURCE_GROUP) \
            --name $(AKS_CLUSTER) \
            --overwrite-existing
          
          kubectl create namespace $(NAMESPACE) --dry-run=client -o yaml | \
            kubectl apply -f -
          
          kubectl label namespace $(NAMESPACE) \
            pr.number=$(PR_NUMBER) \
            pr.created=$(Build.BuildNumber) \
            environment=ephemeral --overwrite
          
          echo "##vso[task.setvariable variable=NAMESPACE;isOutput=true]$(NAMESPACE)"
      name: namespaceInfo

    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Log to Azure Monitor'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          az monitor log-analytics query \
            --workspace $(LOG_WORKSPACE_ID) \
            --query "['EphemeralEnvironmentCreated']" \
            --analytics-duration 1 | tee /dev/stderr

- stage: Deploy
  displayName: 'Deploy Application'
  dependsOn: Provision
  jobs:
  - job: HelmDeploy
    displayName: 'Deploy with Helm'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    steps:
    - task: HelmInstaller@1
      displayName: 'Install Helm'
      inputs:
        helmVersionToInstall: 'latest'

    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Configure AKS Credentials'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          az aks get-credentials \
            --resource-group $(RESOURCE_GROUP) \
            --name $(AKS_CLUSTER) \
            --overwrite-existing

    - task: HelmDeploy@0
      displayName: 'Deploy Helm Chart'
      inputs:
        connectionType: 'Azure Resource Manager'
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        azureResourceGroup: '$(RESOURCE_GROUP)'
        kubernetesCluster: '$(AKS_CLUSTER)'
        namespace: '$(NAMESPACE)'
        chartName: '$(CHART_REPO)/$(CHART_NAME)'
        chartVersion: '$(Build.BuildNumber)'
        releaseName: 'pr-app-$(PR_NUMBER)'
        overrideValues: |
          image.tag=$(Build.BuildNumber)
          ingress.hostname=$(NAMESPACE).$(DOMAIN)

- stage: Test
  displayName: 'Smoke Tests'
  dependsOn: Deploy
  jobs:
  - job: SmokeTests
    displayName: 'Run Smoke Tests'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    steps:
    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Wait for Deployment'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          kubectl wait --for=condition=available \
            --timeout=300s \
            deployment/pr-app-$(PR_NUMBER) \
            -n $(NAMESPACE)

    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Run Smoke Tests'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          SERVICE_IP=$(kubectl get svc -n $(NAMESPACE) \
            -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].ip}')
          
          curl -f http://$SERVICE_IP/health || exit 1
          curl -f http://$SERVICE_IP/api/version || exit 1

- stage: Teardown
  displayName: 'Teardown Environment'
  condition: or(
    eq(variables['Build.Reason'], 'PullRequest'),
    eq(dependencies.Provision.outputs['CreateNamespace.namespaceInfo.namespace'], '')
  )
  jobs:
  - job: DeleteNamespace
    displayName: 'Delete PR Namespace'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    steps:
    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Policy Check Before Deletion'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          NAMESPACE=$(NAMESPACE)
          if [[ "$NAMESPACE" == pr-* ]]; then
            echo "Validating deletion policy for ephemeral namespace..."
            az policy assignment list \
              --scope /subscriptions/$(SUB_ID)/resourceGroups/$(RESOURCE_GROUP) \
              --query "[?displayName=='ProtectEphemeralNamespaces']" | tee /dev/stderr
          else
            echo "##vso[task.logissue type=warning]Non-PR namespace - skipping deletion"
            exit 1
          fi

    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Delete Namespace'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          kubectl delete namespace $(NAMESPACE) --wait=true
          
          echo "Namespace $(NAMESPACE) deleted successfully"

    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Log Deletion to Azure Monitor'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          az monitor metrics alert create \
            --name "namespace-deleted-$(NAMESPACE)" \
            --resource-group $(RESOURCE_GROUP) \
            --description "Ephemeral namespace $(NAMESPACE) has been deleted"

resources:
  webhooks:
  - webhook: PRClosed
    connectionType: 'azureDevOps'
    project: '$(System.TeamProject)'
    pipeline: '$(Build.DefinitionName)'

schedules:
- cron: '0 0 * * *'
  displayName: 'Daily Cleanup'
  branches:
    include:
    - main
  always: true
```

## Key Implementation Details
1. **Namespace Creation**: Dynamically creates pr-${PR_NUMBER} namespace with metadata labels for tracking
2. **Helm Deployment**: Uses HelmDeploy@0 task with Azure Resource Manager connection for secure deployment
3. **Smoke Testing**: Validates application health and API endpoints post-deployment
4. **Policy Protection**: Validates namespace pattern before deletion to prevent accidental removal of non-prod environments
5. **Azure Monitor Logging**: All operations are logged for audit and troubleshooting
6. **Scheduled Cleanup**: Cron job ensures stale environments are removed after 24 hours
7. **Webhook Integration**: Triggers cleanup when PR is merged or closed

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to architect a multi-service, multi-region CI/CD flow in Azure DevOps, including selective builds, secure secret management, per-service approvals, and cross-region canary with rollback.

## Key Concepts

- Mono-repo service-level change detection
- Conditional jobs and environments per service
- Azure Key Vault integration for per-environment secrets
- Region-aware canary deployments via Azure Front Door
- Rollback strategy: redeploy last good artifact and pause production jobs

## Code Example

```yaml
# YAML skeleton (conceptual)
trigger:
  branches:
    include:
      - main
      - develop

variables:
  - group: 'global-config'
  - name: 'changedServices'
    value: ''

stages:
- stage: DetectChanges
  displayName: 'Detect Changed Services'
  jobs:
  - job: Detect
    displayName: 'Detect Changes'
    steps:
    - bash: |
        # Detect changed services using git diff
        changed=$(git diff --name-only $(Build.SourceVersion) $(Build.SourceBranch) | grep -E '^(services/[^/]+)/' | cut -d'/' -f2 | sort -u | tr '\n' ',')
        echo "##vso[task.setvariable variable=changedServices;isOutput=true]${changed%,}"
      name: detectChanges

- stage: BuildAndTest
  displayName: 'Build and Test Services'
  dependsOn: DetectChanges
  condition: ne(dependencies.DetectChanges.outputs['Detect.detectChanges.changedServices'], '')
  jobs:
  - ${{ each service in split(dependencies.DetectChanges.outputs['Detect.detectChanges.changedServices'], ',') }}:
    - job: Build_${{ service }}
      displayName: 'Build ${{ service }}'
      steps:
      - task: DotNetCoreCLI@2
        displayName: 'Build ${{ service }}'
        inputs:
          command: 'build'
          projects: 'services/${{ service }}/*.csproj'
      - task: DotNetCoreCLI@2
        displayName: 'Test ${{ service }}'
        inputs:
          command: 'test'
          projects: 'services/${{ service }}/*.Tests.csproj'

- stage: DeployStaging
  displayName: 'Deploy to Staging'
  dependsOn: BuildAndTest
  jobs:
  - ${{ each service in split(dependencies.DetectChanges.outputs['Detect.detectChanges.changedServices'], ',') }}:
    - deployment: Deploy_${{ service }}_Staging
      displayName: 'Deploy ${{ service }} to Staging'
      environment: '${{ service }}-staging'
      strategy:
        runOnce:
          deploy:
            steps:
            - task: AzureKeyVault@2
              displayName: 'Get Secrets from Key Vault'
              inputs:
                azureSubscription: 'ServiceConnection'
                KeyVaultName: 'kv-${{ service }}-staging'
                SecretsFilter: '*'
            - task: AzureWebApp@1
              displayName: 'Deploy ${{ service }}'
              inputs:
                azureSubscription: 'ServiceConnection'
                appName: 'app-${{ service }}-staging'
                package: '$(Pipeline.Workspace)/drop/${{ service }}.zip'

- stage: DeployProduction
  displayName: 'Deploy to Production'
  dependsOn: DeployStaging
  jobs:
  - ${{ each service in split(dependencies.DetectChanges.outputs['Detect.detectChanges.changedServices'], ',') }}:
    - deployment: Deploy_${{ service }}_Production
      displayName: 'Deploy ${{ service }} to Production'
      environment: '${{ service }}-production'
      strategy:
        canary:
          increments: [10, 50, 100]
          preDeployGate:
            approval: '${{ service }}-prod-approval'
          deployGate:
            approval: '${{ service }}-prod-approval'
      steps:
      - task: AzureKeyVault@2
        displayName: 'Get Production Secrets'
        inputs:
          azureSubscription: 'ServiceConnection'
          KeyVaultName: 'kv-${{ service }}-prod'
          SecretsFilter: '*'
      - task: AzureWebApp@1
        displayName: 'Deploy to Primary Region'
        inputs:
          azureSubscription: 'ServiceConnection'
          appName: 'app-${{ service }}-prod-primary'
          package: '$(Pipeline.Workspace)/drop/${{ service }}.zip'
      - task: AzureWebApp@1
        displayName: 'Deploy to Secondary Region'
        inputs:
          azureSubscription: 'ServiceConnection'
          appName: 'app-${{ service }}-prod-secondary'
          package: '$(Pipeline.Workspace)/drop/${{ service }}.zip'
      - task: AzureFrontDoor@1
        displayName: 'Update Front Door Routing'
        inputs:
          azureSubscription: 'ServiceConnection'
          FrontDoorProfile: 'fd-${{ service }}'
          RoutingRule: '${{ service }}-routing'
          BackendPool: '${{ service }}-backend'
```

## Implementation Notes

- Use `git diff` to detect changed services at the directory level
- Implement conditional stages that only run when services have changed
- Leverage Azure DevOps environments for per-service approval gates
- Configure Azure Key Vault integration with service-specific vaults
- Implement canary deployments with incremental traffic routing
- Use Azure Front Door for region-aware traffic management
- Store rollback artifacts and implement automated rollback triggers
